abstract: This IMF Staff Discussion Note examines skill gaps and job creation in the AI age, analyzing labor market trends across developed economies. The analysis reveals significant wage premiums for positions requiring multiple new skills and demonstrates a growing polarization in the labor market where high-skill workers gain employment advantages while middle-skill roles face compression.
keyFindings: Job postings requiring 4 or more new skills command wage premiums of up to 15% in the UK and 8.5% in the US compared to traditional positions
Middle-skill roles are being squeezed as labor market demand shifts toward both high-skill and low-skill occupations
High-skill workers are experiencing relative gains in employment opportunities and wage growth due to AI-driven transformation
Skills-based wage divergence is accelerating, with significant compensation differences emerging between positions requiring emerging versus traditional competencies
